```{r read in data, message = FALSE}
#data in Draft Rates by property 26.27 - statistical purposes 1 in two sheets. Data and Unit Rates

#===== Read in data ======
Data <- read_excel("Draft Rates by property 26.27 - statistical purposes 1.xlsx", sheet = "Data", skip = 2) %>%
  drop_na(property_no) #first two rows are blank, Can map headers from unit_rates reference data set. Last rows are totals, but totals have no property number, so drop. 
# Unit_Rates <- read_excel("Draft Rates by property 26.27 - statistical purposes 1.xlsx", sheet = "Unit Rates")
wdc_rates <- read_csv("wdc_rates_qv.csv") %>% 
  mutate(rate_yr = factor(rate_yr, levels = c("22_23", "23_24", "24_25", "25_26", "26_27"), ordered = TRUE))

#CPI data for indexing
CPI <- read.csv("CPI.csv") %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date, format = "%d-%m-%Y"),
         year = year(Date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(CPI = mean(CPI..Annual...change.))

#===== map setup begin ======
nz <- read_sf("https://www.massey.ac.nz/~jcmarsha/data/nz_map/sa3_data.sqlite")

ta_nz <- nz %>% 
  group_by(territorial_authority, regional_council) %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_union(GEOMETRY), .groups = 'drop')

whanganui <- nz %>% filter(territorial_authority == "Whanganui District")
bbox <- st_bbox(whanganui)

w_bbox <- list(x = c(1767500, 1779000), y=c(5574000, 5585000))
#===== map setup finish ======

#===== Mapping Suburbs begin =====
St_John_Streets <- c('Acton Pl', 'Aiken Rd', 'Alexa Pl', "Brassey Rd","Bristow St", "Chittick Pl","Collier Pl", "Dickson Cres", "Halswell St","Halswell Street","Hillside Tce", "Kent Rd","Linda Pl", "Ngapuhi St", "Oakland Ave","Parkes Ave", "Parsons St", "Porritt St", "Rawhiti Pl", "Smart Tce", "St Leonard St","Taranaki St","Tarata St", "Tregarth St","Tulloch St", "Virginia Rd", 'Peakes Rd', 'Victoria Park', 'Virginia Lake (Rotokawau)')

Otamatea_Streets <- c('Sewerage Pump Turere', 'Babbage Pl', 'Beachcroft', "Chelsea Cl", "Cotswolds Cl", "Diana Pl", "Eaton Cres", "Edith Collier Dr", "Edmonds Dr", "Goldsbury Pl", "Gumtree Rise", "Holdsworth Dr", "Kawau Pl", "Lancewood Pl", "Lithgow Dr", "Mannington Rd", "Montgomery Rd", "Norfolk Dr", "Otamatea Reserve", "Perrett Dr", "Pickwick Rd", "Rotokawau Dr", "Sandcroft Dr", "Sandy Lane", "St Johns Hts", "Suffolk Dr", "Tasman Views", "Tirimoana Pl", "Turere Pl","Virginia Hts", "Webster Pl", "Pukeko Drive", 'Tangaroa View', 'Middens Way')

Springvale_streets <-c('Addenbrooke Tce')

Whanganui_Centre_Streets <- c('Pitt St', 'Peat Pl', 'Peat St')

#===== Mapping suburbs finish =====

#===== Data wrangling begin =====
streets <- wdc_rates %>% 
  filter(suburb == "St Johns/Otamatea") %>% 
  select(property_no, rate_yr, property_address, suburb) %>%
  mutate(
    house_num = as.integer(str_extract(property_address, "^\\s*(\\d+)")), 
    street = str_remove(property_address, "~.*"),
    street = str_remove(street, "-."),
    street = str_remove(street, "^(?i:unit\\s+)?(?:[\\d/][\\d/A-Za-z]*\\s+)+"), #handles numbers and numbers like 9A,alos UNIT 6C / 59 and
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    suburb = case_when(
      #house numbers on great north road. great north road spans both. Lower number in St Johns up to 117. Then 119 and 121 are St Johns. 118, 120 and 122 onwards are otamtea
      street == "Great North Rd" & is.na(house_num) ~ "St Johns Hill",
      street == "Great North Rd" & house_num <= 117 ~ "St Johns Hill",
      street == "Great North Rd" & house_num %in% c(119, 121) ~ "St Johns Hill",
      street == "Great North Rd" & house_num >= 118 ~ "Otamatea (Whanganui District)",
      #easier ones
      street %in% St_John_Streets ~ "St Johns Hill",
      street %in% Otamatea_Streets ~ "Otamatea (Whanganui District)",
      street %in% Springvale_streets ~ "Springvale",
      street %in% Whanganui_Centre_Streets ~ "Whanganui Centre",
      TRUE ~ suburb
    )
  ) %>% select(property_no, rate_yr, suburb) #for left join

#join tdatasets to get what I need. Remove nulls from data set.
Rates <- wdc_rates %>% 
  filter(!is.na(assessment_number)) %>%
  left_join(
    Data %>% select(property_no, SUIP), 
    by = 'property_no') %>%
  mutate( #mapping qv_category to res/com/farm for simpler groupings
    Category = case_when(
      `qv category` %in% c('Commercial', 'Industrial') ~ 'Commercial', 
      `qv category` %in% c('Farming', 'Dairy', 'Pastoral', 'Forestry', 'Horticulture', 'Mining') ~ 'Farming',
      `qv category` %in% c('Other', 'Specialist', 'Utility asset') ~ 'Specialist',
      `qv category` %in% c('Residential', 'Lifestyle') ~ 'Residential',
      TRUE ~ `qv category`),
    SUIP = case_when(
      `qv category` == 'Mining' ~ 1,
      `qv category` == 'Residential' & is.na(SUIP) ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ SUIP)
    ) %>%
  left_join(streets, by = c('property_no', 'rate_yr'), suffix = c("", "_new")) %>%
  mutate(suburb = coalesce(suburb_new, suburb)) %>%
  mutate(
    suburb = recode(suburb,
    "Bastia/Durie Hills Putiki" = "Bastia-Durie Hill-Putiki",
    "Whanganui Central" = "Whanganui Centre",
    "Whanganui Rural" = "Whanganui District Rural",)
  ) %>%
  mutate(year = case_when(
    rate_yr == '22_23' ~ 2022,
    rate_yr == '23_24' ~ 2023,
    rate_yr == '24_25' ~ 2024,
    rate_yr == '25_26' ~ 2025,
    rate_yr == '26_27' ~ 2026,
    TRUE ~ NA
  )) %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(Category, 
                           levels = c('Specialist', 'Farming', 'Commercial', 'Residential'))) %>% #for consistent color coding
  select(-suburb_new) 
#===== Data wrangling finish =====

#===== Colour palette setup =====
whanganui_palette <- function(n = 13) {
  pal <- c( #from inspecting the page elements of the Whanganui website, then color dropper picking from the coat of arms
  "#2757A2", 
  "#FEC30E",
  "#AD1619",
  "#008242", 
  "#DCC0E2", 
  "#C7E9F3",
  "#004925",
  "#D4582A",
  "#372502",
  "#8B514E",
  "#93735B", 
  "#687928",
  "#FEEAD7")
  if (n <= length(pal)) {
    pal[seq_len(n)]
  } else {
    grDevices::colorRampPalette(pal)(n)
  }
}

#===== Custom theme =====#
# font is Inter sans-serif, from website inspect elements on Whanganui council

theme_report <- function(base_size = 15) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Inter") +
    theme(
      # Titles
      plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0,
                                   margin = margin(b = 5)),
      # Axes
      axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 15),
      # Facet strips
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
      # Legend
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_text(size = 15),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
      # Caption
      plot.caption = element_text(size =15)
    )
}

theme_map <- function(base_size = 15) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Inter") +
    theme(
      # panels
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      # Titles
      plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, hjust = 0),
      # Axes
      axis.title =  element_blank(),
      axis.text =  element_blank(),
      # Legend
      legend.title = element_text(size = 15),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 15)
    )
}
```

# Graph 0: rates over time vs RBNZ inflation
```{r graph 0, fig.width = 10, fig.height=5}
#RBNZ data I just copied from their website. Didn't seem like worth all the effort to download the full dataset.Rate yaers frun from start july to end June (source: my ever increasing rates bill :( )
#NZ financial year is from start march to end april, so I need to get the NZ rates year quarter inflation values to map the rates to inflation correctly

#RBNZ pink #ed1166
RBNZ_inflation <- CPI %>% filter(year >= 2022)
CPI_2022 <- RBNZ_inflation %>% filter(year == 2022) %>% pull(CPI)

#indexing rates to inflations, then getting % change ot compare next to CPI
timeseries_data <- Rates %>% #filter(Category == 'Residential') %>%
  arrange(property_no, year) %>%
  left_join(RBNZ_inflation, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(indexed_rates = (`total rates` / CPI) * CPI_2022) %>%
  group_by(property_no) %>%
  mutate(pct_change = (indexed_rates - lag(indexed_rates)) / lag(indexed_rates) * 100,
         pct_change = replace_na(pct_change, 0)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(property_no, year, `total rates`, indexed_rates, pct_change, Category)

G0_data <- timeseries_data %>%
  group_by(Category, year) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct_change = mean(pct_change), .groups = 'drop') 

G0_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = mean_pct_change, x = year, col = Category)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2,show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(data = RBNZ_inflation, aes(y = CPI, x = year, color = "RBNZ Inflation Rate"), linewidth = 1, linetype= 'dashed') +
  geom_point(data = RBNZ_inflation, aes(y = CPI, x = year, color = "RBNZ Inflation Rate"), size = 2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  #Scale arguments
  scale_x_continuous(labels = x_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(round(min(G0_data$mean_pct_change),0), 
                                  round(max(G0_data$mean_pct_change),0)),
                      breaks = scales::breaks_width(10)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    setNames(whanganui_palette[1:4], c('Specialist', 'Farming', 'Commercial', 'Residential')),
    "RBNZ Inflation Rate" = "#ed1166"),
    name= "Legend") +
  #labels
  labs(title = 'Whanganui year on year mean rate percentage change against RBNZ CPI',
       subtitle = 'Rates changes are usually higher than CPI, except for 2026/27',
       x = '',
       y ='%',
       color = 'Legend',
       caption = 'Rate values have been index linked to 2022 inflation in order to compare like.' ) +
  #theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = 'top',
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank())

```

#Graph 1: rates by category
Residential rate payers as a group pay the highest amount of rates, \$80,892,140$ in total. 
However, the median rates for residential payers is \$4,003.52, compared to \$7,344.46 of commercial rate payers. 
Specialist rate payers pay the least at \$2,297.72, while Farming rate payers pay a median of \$3,403.05. 
Residential rate payers rates vary the least between the interquartile range.
So, while they vary less and pay less in general, because they are the largest category, they pay the most rates. Despite the commercial category paying higher per rating unit.

#Graph 2: Residential rates change  through time. % change

```{r graphn 2, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
#===== ribbon chart =====#
#redline shows median change
ribbon_chart <- timeseries_data %>%
  group_by(year, Category) %>%
  median_qi(pct_change, .width = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = pct_change, ymin = .lower, ymax = .upper, color = Category)) +
  geom_lineribbon(color = "#DC0100", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.7) + #from the vignette https://mjskay.github.io/ggdist/articles/lineribbon.html
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 2023), linetype ='dashed') + 
  facet_wrap(~ Category, scales = "free_y") +
  #scales
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#C7E9F3", "#92B8D8", "#5C88BD","#2757A2"),
                    name = 'Quantile') +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = x_labels) +
  #labels
  labs(title = 'Inflation indexed residential rates change year on year',
     subtitle = 'Rate % change varied the most in the 2023/24 year, when the 2022 QV revaluation was applied.\nResidential rates have varied the least.',
     y = 'Percentage change', 
     x = '') +
  #Theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = 'top',
        panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

#===== Cumulative percent change =====#
cumulative_data <- timeseries_data %>%
  group_by(year, Category) %>%
  summarise(pct_change = mean(pct_change), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  arrange(year) %>% #should be arranged already... paranoid
  mutate(cum_chg = cumsum(pct_change))

avg_cum_perc <- cumulative_data %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(avg = mean(cum_chg))

cumulative_chart <- cumulative_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, col = Category)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cum_chg), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = avg_cum_perc, aes(x = year, y = avg, col = 'Average'),
            linewidth = 1, linetype = 'dashed') +
  #scales
  scale_x_continuous(labels = x_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(round(min(cumulative_data$cum_chg),0), 
                                round(max(cumulative_data$cum_chg),0)),
                    breaks = scales::breaks_width(10)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
      setNames(whanganui_palette[1:4], c('Specialist', 'Farming', 'Commercial', 'Residential')),
      "Average" = "black")) +
  #labels
  labs(
    title = 'Cumulatively, residential rates have changed the least',
    subtitle = "Consistently just below the average",
    x = '',
    y = 'Percent'
  ) +
  #theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = 'top',
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

#patchwork output together
(ribbon_chart / cumulative_chart)
  
  
```

Residential rates change the most in terms of median % change. 


# Graph 3 - Map
For the year 2026/27, within the residential rates category, the highest median rates are paid in the Otamatea suburb (\$5,213.6), but the least total rates (\$3,090,701). Otamatea has the highest valued houses, but the fewest houses (593), this is why. Gonville, on the other hand pays the most total rates (\$12,198,414), but one of the lowest medians rates ($3928,71). Gonville has the most houses (2916) of any suburb. 
We can see that price is not a funciton of units in a suburb. fewer houses does not = higher price 


```{r graph 4 map, fig.width=15, fig.height=8}
#===== Map Graph function =====#
map_graph <- function(data, fill, title) {
data %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(mapping=aes(fill = .data[[fill]]), col = 'white', linewidth = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_sf(xlim = w_bbox$x, ylim = w_bbox$y) + #need to change the rural district label to be visible
  #annotation
  geom_sf_label(mapping = aes(label = paste0(sa3_name, "\nn= ",as.character(count))), 
               size = 3) + 
  annotate("label", x = 1777000, y = 5584000,
           label = paste0("Rural\nn=", rural_count), 
           size = 3, fill = 'white') + #play with this to get the position right
  #Scale arguments
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = c("#008242", "#FEC30E", "#AD1619"),
                       limits = range(data[[fill]]),
                       name = title) +
  #Labels
  labs(title = title,
       subtitle = '',
       x = '',
       y = '') +
  #Theme
  theme_map()
}
#===== Wrangling =====#
graph_3_data <- Rates %>% 
  filter(year == 2026, Category == 'Residential') %>%
  group_by(suburb) %>%
  summarise(median_rates = median(`total rates`),
            count = n(),
            total = sum(`total rates`),
            .groups = 'drop')

map_data <- whanganui %>%
  left_join(graph_3_data, by = c('sa3_name' = "suburb")) %>%
  mutate(sa3_name = recode(sa3_name, 
                           "Otamatea (Whanganui District)" = "Otamatea"))

#get count of units in suburb for labels
#this is separate because the labels wants to be out of the bounding box window
rural_count <- graph_3_data %>%
  filter(suburb == 'Whanganui District Rural') %>%
  pull(count)

#===== Median rates map =====#
median_map <- map_graph(map_data, "median_rates", 'Median rates')

#===== total rates map =====#

#patchwork the plot together.
(median_map | total_map) +
  plot_annotation(title = 'Residential rates in year 2026/27.',
                  subtitle = 'Otamatea has the highest residential rates, Gonville pays the most rates in total.',
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 30),
                                plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 20)))
```

#Who pays the most?
So, who pays the most in residential rates? Proportionally, it is Otamatea rates payers. Their payments are larger than other rates payers not just in value, but also relative to all rates payers. Proportionally, the median is around 0.006 from 2023 onwards Even if they pay less as a combined group. St John's hill comes in second at 0.0059. Rural rate payers pay the least, at 0.0042. Note the quantile intervals. Central has the highest rateable units as outliers, while Otamatea has a few low valued outliers. There is overlap in each suburb with each other suburb. In general, the observation holds. Higher median rate paying suburbs pay more than their "fair" share. Obviously, "fair" here is a construct. Rates are not even, they are based off of QV value and SUIPs. 


```{r graph 4, fig.width=15, fig.height=8}

equal_prop <- residential %>%

  tidyr::crossing(suburb = unique(residential$suburb))

prop_data <- residential %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(prop = 100 * `total rates` / sum(`total rates`)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(year, suburb) %>%
  reframe(median_qi(prop, .width = c(.25, .50, .80, .95)))

#ranking suburbs
suburb_rank <- prop_data %>%
  filter(year == 2026, .width == 0.50) %>%
  mutate(rank = rank(-y, ties.method = "min")) %>%
  arrange(rank)

#final data
graph_4_data <- prop_data %>%
  left_join(suburb_rank %>% select(suburb, rank), by = "suburb") %>%
  mutate(suburb_ranked = factor(
    paste0(suburb, ", rank ", rank),
    levels = paste0(suburb_rank$suburb, ", rank ", suburb_rank$rank)
  ))

#==== Graph ====#
graph_4_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = y)) +
  geom_lineribbon(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                  color = "#DC0100", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = equal_prop, aes(x = year, y = prop),
            col = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ suburb_ranked, ncol = 5) +
  #scale arguments
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) x %% 100) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#C7E9F3", "#92B8D8", "#5C88BD","#2757A2"),
                    name = "Quantiles") +
  #labels
  labs(title = "Otamatea rate payers pay proportionally the most rates",
       subtitle = "The four more expensive suburbs pay proportionally more rates than cheaper ones.",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Proportion of rates paid per unit",
       caption = "Black dotted line is the proportion if every house paid the same share towards rates.") +
  #themes
  theme_report() 
```


#Graph 4 - rain clouds by SUIP

Show rates by group
and proportional rates. To  show that commericals pays more in prop than residentail. 

Are the rich contributing? Look at total rates paid by residential suburb
Maybe look at the stat half eye by subrub actual rates?
what about the SUIPs.

only 779 units have 3+ SUIPs



```{r, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}
# for one graph I will show, with the density eye plot the categorical density of rates by qv category. As they vary heaps
# lots of categories, maybe too many. I'll try mapping them ot the Data res/com/faarm ones ot get a clearer graph
widths = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95)

#identify outliers by category, then also plot them on the graph., Use a simple IQR method

graph_5_data <- Rates %>% 
  filter(Category == 'Residential', !is.na(SUIP), year == 2026) %>%
  arrange(SUIP) %>%
  mutate(SUIP_grp = case_when(
    SUIP == 0 ~ '0 ',
    SUIP == 1 ~ '1 ',
    SUIP == 2 ~ '2 ', 
    SUIP >= 3 ~ '3+'
    ),
    SUIP_grp = factor(SUIP_grp, levels = rev(c('0 ', '1 ', '2 ', '3+')))) %>%
  mutate(
    fct_grp = case_when(
      SUIP_grp == "3+" ~ 2,
      TRUE ~ 1
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(SUIP_grp) %>%
  mutate(title = paste0(trimws(as.character(SUIP_grp)),
                        " (n = ", n(), ")")) %>%
  ungroup()

median_SUIP <- graph_5_data %>% summarise(median(`total rates`)) %>% pull()

rain_clouds <- graph_5_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `total rates`, y = SUIP_grp, fill = SUIP_grp)) +
  stat_halfeye(
    mapping = aes(fill_ramp = after_stat(level)),
    fill_type = "segments",
    .width = widths,
    adjust = 3, 
    alpha = 0.5,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    col = 'grey33',
  ) +
  stat_dotsinterval(
    mapping = aes(fill_ramp = after_stat(level)),
    .width = widths,
    side = "bottom",
    layout = 'weave',
    scale = 0.5,
    slab_linewidth = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    quantiles = 50) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = median_SUIP), col = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ fct_grp, nrow = 2, scales = "free") +
  #scales
  scale_fill_manual(values = whanganui_palette(4)) +
  scale_fill_ramp_discrete(na.translate = FALSE) +
  scale_y_discrete(
  labels = set_names( #get the order for the title back
    graph_5_data %>% distinct(SUIP_grp, title) %>% pull(title),
    graph_5_data %>% distinct(SUIP_grp, title) %>% pull(SUIP_grp)
  )) +
  #labels
  labs(
    title = "More SUIPs means more rates.",
    subtitle = "Most residential units have one SUIP, set exactly at the median rate value (dashed line).",
    y = "",
    x = "Total rates per unit",
    caption = "3+ SUIPs have many more outliers, and have been split to a separate set of axes."
  ) +
  #theme
  theme_report() +
  theme(strip.text = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1))


```

```{r}
                         "Whanganui District Rural" = "Rural",

       subtitle = '',
       x = '',

  #Theme
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = 'right')
```
